answer: New agents may enter only through a capacity-limited inlet that admits a fixed number of identities per epoch. Each admitted agent must post a walnut bond, locked until it finishes several uncorrelated work windows. If later audits show shared countersigners, timing, or infrastructure, those bonds are slashed together and leftover standing is collapsed onto one dune that then decays. An attacker therefore buys a scarce inlet slot and locks a distinct bond for every fake identity, and still loses the cluster's entire stake and weight when correlation is found.
